faqs.a:
The admissions tax imposed pursuant to this article, together with all interest and
               penalties pertaining thereto, shall be a first and prior lien on tangible personal
               property in which the person responsible to collect and remit the admissions tax has
               an ownership interest, subject only to a perfected security interest. The finance
               director may also treat admissions taxes and penalties or interest due thereon and
               then paid as a debt due to the city from any person subject to the provisions of this
               article, which shall be recoverable by the city in an action at law.
(Code 1981, § 31-142; Ord. No. 3783, § 2, 12-16-2002)
